results.summary: AI's shift from training to inference is driving rapid and accelerating growth in memory demand, particularly HBM.
results.quote: rapid growth in memory demand driven by AI's shift from training to inference
results.evidence: The article explicitly names 'Gavin Baker, CIO and Managing Partner of Atreides Management' as the speaker presenting these insights at the 2025 Sohn Montreal Conference, and a self-identifying turn notes Baker thanking the Sohn Foundation and preferring to sit.

results.summary: SK Hynix is the dominant HBM supplier and offers ~3x upside as the primary beneficiary of AI inference-driven memory demand.
results.quote: 3X Upside Riding the AI Inference Wave with a Dominant HBM Supplier
results.evidence: The article headline and body directly attribute the '3X Upside' HBM thesis to Gavin Baker of Atreides Management presenting at Sohn Montreal 2025, with Baker identified by name as the sole presenter.

results.summary: Reasoning models (advanced inference-time compute scaling) are a structural catalyst for HBM demand growth beyond what consensus expects.
results.quote: advancements in reasoning models and high-bandwidth memory are reshaping the semiconductor landscape
results.evidence: The article explicitly states Baker 'highlighted how advancements in reasoning models and high-bandwidth memory are reshaping the semiconductor landscape,' directly attributing this framing to him by name.
